clue.text: Thinking that's arresting!

explanation.surface: An exclamation that some thought is striking.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the word as DE-LIBERATING: taking away someone's liberty, which is what an arrest does.
explanation.definitionFit: Deliberating is weighing something up in the mind; read as de-liberating, it means removing freedom, as police do when they arrest someone.

clue.text: Designers of storage furniture

explanation.surface: People who design cupboards and chests.
explanation.definitionFit: People who draw plans are drawers, and drawers are also the sliding boxes in a chest or desk.

clue.text: Settled about a motorway restriction

indicators.note: about means the first word's letters go around the second piece here

parts.note: a bird that has settled on a branch has lit there
the M1 is Britain's first motorway, written here as MI

explanation.surface: A speed limit or ban imposed along a motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1, the motorway from London to Leeds, is read as the letters MI.
explanation.definitionFit: A limit is a cap or boundary, the same thing as a restriction.

clue.text: Players getting on in years, and so wrapping up well

parts.note: a band is a group of musical players
growing old, i.e. aging

explanation.surface: Elderly musicians wrap up warmly against the cold.
explanation.definitionFit: Bandaging is wrapping a wound up properly in dressings.

clue.text: Speed and incur censure!

explanation.surface: An order to drive fast and get into trouble for it.
explanation.definitionFit: A rate is a pace or velocity; to rate, in an older sense, is to scold, the reproof one incurs.

clue.text: A neat fighter has to study the alternative

parts.note: to read a subject is to study it
the word introducing an alternative is or

explanation.surface: A tidy boxer must also learn about the other option.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Neat' is an old word for cattle, so a neat fighter fights bulls; it is not about tidiness.
explanation.definitionFit: A bullfighter on foot is a toreador, and neat means cattle or oxen.

clue.text: A woman with no aim to appear made-up

indicators.note: made-up says the letters of the words no aim are invented anew in a different order

explanation.surface: An aimless woman trying to look made-up with cosmetics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made-up' suggests make-up on a face but signals rearranging the letters of NO AIM.
explanation.definitionFit: Naomi is a female given name, borne by the mother-in-law of Ruth in the Bible.

clue.text: Block outside broadcast, cutting returns in a way

indicators.note: in places the turned piece inside the abbreviation for a way

parts.note: ST is short for street, a way

indicators.note: returns means the synonym for cutting is read backwards

parts.note: a cutting remark is curt

explanation.surface: A TV outside broadcast held up by cuts to its earnings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' turns CURT into TRUC, which 'in' places inside ST, giving STRUCT after OB.
explanation.definitionFit: To obstruct is to block or bar the way.

clue.text: Some youngster needing help to become a writer

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A young person who needs assistance to become an author.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition took in 'help to become', which no novelist means; 'help to become' is a link, so the definition is 'a writer'. Laurence Sterne wrote Tristram Shandy.
explanation.definitionFit: Laurence Sterne was an eighteenth-century novelist, author of Tristram Shandy.

clue.text: Carpet with cross laid in a cathedral

indicators.note: laid in says the cross is placed inside the words for a cathedral

parts.note: a minster is a large church or cathedral, so a minster
X is the shape of a cross

explanation.surface: A carpet with a cross pattern laid in a cathedral aisle.
explanation.walkthrough: Axminster is a Devon town famous for its woven carpets.
explanation.definitionFit: An Axminster is a type of machine-woven tufted rug.

clue.text: A round gold piece

parts.note: or is the heraldic word for gold
a bit is a piece

explanation.surface: Describing a circular gold coin.
explanation.definitionFit: An orbit is one circuit or revolution, a round.

clue.text: Catch comrade almost retreating

indicators.note: retreating says the shortened word goes backwards
almost means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a partner is a companion or comrade

explanation.surface: Nearly catching a friend who is running away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims PARTNER to PARTNE, which 'retreating' turns back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: To entrap is to snare or capture by trickery.

clue.text: The vessel is Cretan possibly

indicators.note: possibly says the letters of is Cretan may be arranged another way

explanation.surface: An ancient pot said to be from Crete.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cretan' suggests an ancient jar from Crete but is simply fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A canister is a small container, a vessel for holding tea or film.

clue.text: Air pressure

explanation.surface: Atmospheric pressure, as in weather.
explanation.definitionFit: A strain is a tune or melody, and strain is also stress or tension.

clue.text: Most enthusiastic about a new diet's composition

parts.note: re means about or concerning

indicators.note: new says the letters of a and diet's are made into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Most keen on the makeup of a fresh diet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges A DIETS to ADIEST; 'composition' only extends the anagram's sense.
explanation.definitionFit: The readiest person is the most willing or eager.

clue.text: Where to follow the MPs in disfavour

definitions.note: the noun stands for this phrase through the idiom of being 'in the' kennel

parts.note: to dog someone is to follow them
the House of Commons is the chamber where MPs sit

explanation.surface: Where to trail Members of Parliament who are out of favour.
explanation.walkthrough: Being 'in the doghouse' is an idiom for being in disgrace.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone in the kennel of the idiom is out of favour, disgraced.

clue.text: Equipment for a quadruped stronger than a mule

definitions.text: Equipment for a quadruped stronger than a mule

parts.words: Equipment for a quadruped stronger than a mule
parts.note: reads as a beast tougher than a mule, but a mule is also a backless slipper, so this is footwear sturdier than a slipper fitted to a four-legged animal

explanation.surface: Gear for a beast of burden tougher than a mule.
explanation.walkthrough: A mule is also a backless slipper; an iron shoe for a horse is far sturdier.
explanation.definitionFit: The U-shaped iron nailed to a hoof is the gear for a four-legged animal.

clue.text: Though a drinker, the driver should imbibe nothing

indicators.note: should imbibe means the driver's word takes in the letter for nothing

parts.note: a car user is a driver
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A driver who likes a drink should take no alcohol.
explanation.walkthrough: 'imbibe' suggests drinking but places O inside CAR USER.
explanation.definitionFit: A carouser is one who drinks heavily and merrily.

clue.text: Press men at one time in China

explanation.surface: Newspapermen once based in China.
explanation.definitionFit: To shanghai is to press-gang sailors, as was done in the past; the city of that name is a port in China.

clue.text: March exercises on the Plain

parts.note: to march is to step
PE is physical education, exercises

explanation.surface: Soldiers march through drills on open grassland.
explanation.definitionFit: The steppe is the vast grassland of Russia and Central Asia.

clue.text: Tropical plant study must include pollution

indicators.note: must include says the word for study goes around the word for pollution

parts.note: to con is to study or learn by heart
rot is decay or corruption, pollution

explanation.surface: Research on a tropical plant must take account of pollution.
explanation.definitionFit: Croton is a genus of tropical shrubs and trees.

clue.text: Bearing a perfume that is not yet mature

parts.note: N, north, is a compass bearing
a scent is a perfume

explanation.surface: Having a fragrance that has not fully developed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bearing' reads as carrying but is a compass point.
explanation.definitionFit: Nascent means just beginning to exist, still developing.

clue.text: Notice perhaps about half-a-dozen turning out

indicators.note: about here means the shuffled letters go around the Roman numeral
perhaps says the letters of Notice could be arranged otherwise

parts.note: VI is six in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A notice probably sent to some six people being thrown out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' turns NOTICE into ECTION, which 'about' wraps round VI.
explanation.definitionFit: An eviction is the act of throwing a tenant out of a home.

clue.text: Charges could well be dropped regretfully

explanation.surface: Accusations might be withdrawn with regret.
explanation.definitionFit: To tear is to rush, so tears are charges; tears are also shed from the eyes in sorrow.

clue.text: Makes use of foil for certain enclosures

explanation.surface: Using kitchen foil for some containers.
explanation.definitionFit: One who fences wields a foil, the sword of the sport; fences also enclose fields.

clue.text: Showing concern without opposing cut

indicators.note: without in the old sense of outside means the word for concern goes round the letter

parts.note: care is concern
v, for versus, means against or opposing

explanation.surface: Showing concern for others without hostility.
explanation.definitionFit: To carve is to cut into shape or slices.

clue.text: This architect would naturally include flying buttresses

definitions.text: This architect would naturally include flying buttresses

parts.words: This architect would naturally include flying buttresses
parts.note: reads as a builder of Gothic churches, but the architect shares a name with a small bird, which naturally flies

explanation.surface: A cathedral architect who would use flying buttresses.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Christopher Wren designed St Paul's Cathedral; the wren is also a tiny bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Christopher Wren is the famous English architect, and his surname is a bird that flies.

clue.text: Persian leader remains with a Turkish officer

indicators.note: leader means the opening letter of the word Persian

parts.note: ash is what remains after burning

explanation.surface: A Persian chief's remains lie beside an Ottoman officer.
explanation.definitionFit: A pasha was a high-ranking Ottoman official or military commander.

clue.text: Extra money's required for the cleaner beset by inflation

indicators.note: beset by says the cleaner is surrounded by the word for inflation

parts.note: a surge is a swelling or inflation
a char is a cleaning lady in British usage

explanation.surface: Inflation means paying extra for the cleaning lady.
explanation.walkthrough: A char, or charwoman, is a British term for a cleaner.
explanation.definitionFit: A surcharge is an additional fee or charge.

clue.text: Get mean — stern — awkward, causing disaffection

indicators.note: awkward says the letters of get mean stern are jumbled clumsily

explanation.surface: Being mean and stern and awkward causes alienation.
explanation.definitionFit: Estrangement is alienation, a loss of friendly feeling.
